symptom: a sore throat that suddenly made it hard to swallow
hook: a thumb was stuck inside the throat
whatYouSee: The epiglottis is swollen into a rounded thumb shape that narrows the airway.
whyItMatters: Supraglottitis can progress fast and block the airway completely.
treatment: Securing the airway comes first. Treatment includes intravenous antibiotics, steroids, and nebulised adrenaline.
takeaway: A thumb shaped epiglottis on a neck X-ray is an airway emergency.

findings: Lateral projection radiograph of the cervical spine including the lower skull base, mandible, and upper thoracic inlet
Seven cervical vertebrae are visible; overall cervical lordosis appears reduced or straightened
Vertebral body heights appear maintained without obvious anterior wedging or compression fracture
Disc spaces appear relatively preserved at all levels with no gross disc space narrowing
Facet joints and posterior elements appear intact without obvious subluxation or perching
No prevertebral soft tissue swelling is identified; the prevertebral soft tissue contour appears within normal limits
The atlanto-dental interval appears within normal limits
Occiput-C1 and C1-C2 relationships appear grossly preserved
Hyoid bone is visible and appears intact
Calcification or ossification is noted in the region of the posterior oropharyngeal soft tissues superiorly, possibly representing calcified lymph nodes or stylohyoid ligament calcification
No obvious cortical disruption, lytic lesion, or sclerotic lesion is identified in the visualized vertebral bodies
Lower cervical and upper thoracic region is partially obscured by shoulder superimposition
differential: Cervical muscle spasm or positional straightening of normal lordosis (most common cause of lordosis loss on lateral cervical radiograph)
Early degenerative cervical spondylosis (reduced lordosis with incipient disc space changes)
Stylohyoid ligament calcification / Eagle syndrome variant (accounting for the soft tissue calcification seen superiorly)
anatomyConcerns: Shoulder superimposition limits evaluation of C6-C7 and C7-T1 junction; lower cervical levels are not fully visualized
Slight rotation of the cervical spine is suggested by incomplete superimposition of the facet joints bilaterally, which could artifactually affect assessment of alignment
The mouth is open, which is appropriate for a lateral projection but may indicate this was obtained as part of an odontoid or trauma series rather than a standard lateral alone
